StackType.rationale: PowerStackType.Counter. The sim has no StackType concept; Power.on_stack (powers.py:137-139) adds unconditionally, which is what PowerCmd.ModifyAmount does (PowerCmd.cs:236 -- no StackType branch). Third-file citations, not hashed here.

ShouldFlush.issue: Closed 2026-07-27: turn_structure G4 is fixed at the site this entry is the trigger surface for. combat.py:1793 calls `self.player.discard_hand(flush=self.hooks.should_flush_hand())` instead of guarding the whole call, and `discard_hand` (player.py:420-465) treats flush=False as 'every card is retained' -- it skips the move and still runs the tail, `end_of_turn_cleanup()` -- which is FlushPlayerHand's false-arm (CombatManager.cs:1327-1346). RE-READ THIS PASS: the record's claim that the tail also calls `hooks.on_hand_emptied` is now WRONG -- the CURRENT docstring says explicitly 'No `on_hand_emptied` here either', citing CombatManager.cs:880-883's own exclusion of the flush from CheckForEmptyHand, and turn_structure G16 as the finding that removed it (the sim used to fire it from here and that was the bug, not the absence). So `discard_hand` calls no hook at all in its tail now, only `end_of_turn_cleanup()`. Residual explicitly NOT part of this entry and still open at turn_structure G4: the sim has no `after_flush` dispatch at all (executed grep: zero hits in sts2_rl/).

AfterSideTurnEnd.issue: Closed 2026-08-01 (tier-2 round 13): FIXED. The tick moved from on_enemy_side_end (Hook.AfterTurnEnd for the ENEMY side, which an extra player turn never reaches) to after_player_turn_end, matching RetainHandPower.cs:28-34 / CombatManager.cs:1307's PLAYER-side timing. An extra turn now ticks it as C# does. The reasoning replaced: the record's assumption that the two side-end slots were interchangeable.  The text it replaced read: NARROWED 2026-07-27, and the reason it stands has changed. THE ROOT CAUSE NAMED HERE IS FIXED: `should_take_extra_turn` moved to combat.py:823, AFTER `on_player_turn_end`, `_process_turn_end_cards`, the flush and `after_player_turn_end` (:793-809) -- turn_structure G3, mirroring SwitchFromPlayerToEnemySide (CombatManager.cs:1360-1373). But this power still ticks from `on_enemy_side_end` (powers.py:3542-3543), and an extra turn still skips that, because combat.py:823-831 returns before `_execute_enemy_turn`. So the executed witness stands -- one end_turn with a should_take_extra_turn listener leaves Retain Hand(1) on the player where C# has already decremented at :1307 -- and this entry's closing sentence, that 'moving the tick to after_player_turn_end would NOT fix it', is now FALSE: that slot is exactly what would fix it. VERIFIED by reading combat.py:781-833 and powers.py.

guards.rationale: RE-READ THIS PASS: the tick's slot changed again since this rationale was written (see the AfterSideTurnEnd entry's own 2026-08-01 close) -- it now lives on `after_player_turn_end`, which DOES take a `player` argument, and the guard `if player is self.owner:` (powers.py:4453) is the direct port of `participants.Contains(base.Owner)`. So the sim's slot no longer lacks the filter C# needs; it has it, expressed the same way every other player-side AfterSideTurnEnd listener in this batch expresses it.

The sim's Power._tick (powers.py:170-176) decrements the field and _expires at <= 0 where C# routes through PowerCmd.Decrement -> ModifyAmount -> ShouldRemoveDueToAmount (PowerCmd.cs:215-250) -- Decrement, not TickDownDuration, so neither side honours SkipNextDurationTick. Observationally identical for a Buff: ModifyAmount's only unconditional modifier leg is Hook.ModifyPowerAmountReceived (PowerCmd.cs:234), whose ported listeners are ArtifactPower (Debuff-only) and RuinedHelmet (StrengthPower-only). Same mechanism and same verdict as audit/records/power/colossus.json's AfterSideTurnEnd guard, per binding rule 3.

guards.what: Interaction with the per-card Retain keyword
guards.rationale: The sim's discard_hand keeps cards with `card.should_retain_this_turn` (player.py:461,464; renamed from the `card.retain` this rationale used to cite) independently of this power, which is C#'s per-card ShouldRetainThisTurn path. Two independent mechanisms on both sides; this power's false ShouldFlush short-circuits the whole flush, so the per-card path is moot when it is active.
